simple.lightLabel: Wait for a dip, don't chase
simple.headline: Nifty jumped 710 points in two days to 25,938; big traders are betting it won't fall, so buy a dip but don't chase.
simple.do: Wait for Nifty to dip to 25,800–25,850 and hold above 25,800 for a full 15-minute candle, then buy; take profit at 25,950, or square by 3:25 pm.
simple.dont: Don't buy above 26,000; 211,000 bets say it stays under that line today. Don't sell just because it has run up; Thursday's sellers lost big.
simple.stop: If a 15-minute candle closes below 25,750 or above 26,080, close everything and stay out for the day.

trade.name: Makes money if Nifty stays above 25,700 till Tuesday 1 Dec
legs: SELL 1 lot  Nifty 1-Dec  25,700 PE  at about ₹133
BUY  1 lot  Nifty 1-Dec  25,500 PE  at about ₹85
trade.maxLoss: The most you can lose: ₹9,880 (152 points × 65)
trade.when: Only after Nifty dips to 25,800–25,850 and holds above 25,800 for a full 15-minute candle; the puts will be a little dearer then, which is fine. Wednesday's old call spread expires today at its full loss; leave it.
trade.exit: Close both legs if a 15-minute candle closes below 25,750, or once you have kept half of the ₹3,120.

why: On Friday big traders placed 680,000 new bets that Nifty won't fall, far more than the bets that it won't rise; that is why we buy dips, not sell.
The biggest bet nearby, 211,000 contracts expiring today, says it stays under 26,000; so don't buy near that line.
Big traders hold 213,000 bets that it won't fall below 25,500, so a drop usually slows there; the trade sells a put above that cushion.
Option prices point to a move of about 150 points either way today, so 25,800 to 26,050 covers Monday.
simple.risk: Trade one lot only. ₹9,880 is the most you can lose, three times the ₹3,120 you collect, so honour the 25,750 stop. After a 710-point run a sharp pullback is the danger. Paper-trade two weeks before real money.
glossary: PE / put option
A bet that Nifty will fall. Buying one pays if it falls; selling one pays you upfront and costs you if it falls.
CE / call option
A bet that Nifty will rise.
Lot
Nifty options trade in lots of 65 units. ₹1 of option price = ₹65 per lot.
Put spread
Sell one put, buy a cheaper one below it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
15-min candle close
Wait for the 15-minute bar on the chart to finish before acting, so one spike doesn't fool you.
Call spread
Sell one call, buy a cheaper one above it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
Iron condor
A call spread and a put spread sold together. You collect both premiums; it pays if Nifty stays between the two sold strikes, and the loss is capped.

Floor (23-Nov): nothing near spot; 64,600 PE 6.7K is the largest put within 500 points. 63,000 PE 49.8K (+30K Friday) is the month's floor, 62,000 PE 36.6K and 61,000 PE 36.5K below. Near-spot PCR 0.69.

Flow: PCR 1.37 from far-below puts; above 64,600 calls outnumber puts 7 to 1. Spot sits 2,407 above max pain 62,500, which no longer matters today. Expiry-day put IV 56 vs call 14. VIX 17.18. No futures print.

December (29-Dec): PCR 0.94, max pain 63,000. 65,000 CE 49.9K is the wall; 65,000 PE 30.9K (+72) and 64,000 PE 10.4K (+93, the day's biggest add) the near floors; 67,000 CE 27.2K and 70,000 CE 22.0K above. Straddle 2,683 → ±2,280.
Pricing: 65,100 straddle 576 → ±490 by today's close, so 64,420–65,400 is the priced range. The expiry-day 65,000/65,200 call spread pays ≈110 (380−270) against ≈90 of risk; breakeven 65,110.

plan.text: Chasing above 65,000 after a 2,870-point run. Buying 65,000 CE (380) outright on expiry day. Naked writes. Wednesday's 62,300/62,500 call spread sits at its full loss; it expires today.

current.risk: The lean-down call lost: Wednesday's spread hit its full 129-point loss. A monthly expiry after a 4.6% two-day run can squeeze through 65,000 or drop 500 in an hour; defined risk only. Record 15-6, 1 open. Paper.

simple.lightLabel: Wait for a dip, don't chase
simple.headline: Bank Nifty jumped 2,870 points in two days to 64,907; big traders are betting it won't fall, so buy a dip, don't chase.
simple.do: Wait for Bank Nifty to dip to 64,500–64,650 and hold above 64,500 for a full 15-minute candle, then buy; take profit at 64,900, or square by 3:25 pm.
simple.dont: Don't buy above 65,000; 34,000 bets say it stays under that line today. Don't sell just because it has run up; Thursday's sellers lost big.
simple.stop: If a 15-minute candle closes below 64,450 or above 65,150, close everything and stay out of Bank Nifty for the day.

trade.name: Makes money if Bank Nifty closes below 65,000 today
legs: SELL 1 lot  Bank Nifty 23-Nov  65,000 CE  at about ₹380
BUY  1 lot  Bank Nifty 23-Nov  65,200 CE  at about ₹270
trade.maxLoss: The most you can lose: ₹2,700 (90 points × 30)
trade.when: Only after Bank Nifty rises towards 65,000 and a full 15-minute candle fails to close above 65,050; these contracts expire at 3:30 pm today. Wednesday's old call spread expires today at its full loss; leave it.
trade.exit: Close both legs if a 15-minute candle closes above 65,150, or once you have kept half of the ₹3,300; anything left expires at 3:30 pm.

why: On Friday big traders placed 210,000 new bets that Bank Nifty won't fall, far more than the bets that it won't rise; that is why we buy dips, not sell.
The biggest bet nearby, 34,000 contracts expiring today, says it stays under 65,000; that is why the trade sells that line.
Big traders hold 50,000 bets that it won't fall below 63,000, so a drop usually slows there; take profit well before it.
Option prices point to a move of about 490 points either way today, so 64,500 to 65,300 covers Monday.
simple.risk: Trade one lot only. ₹2,700 is the most you can lose, less than the ₹3,300 you collect, but it is lost in one 200-point push above 65,000 on expiry day. Honour the 65,150 stop. Paper-trade two weeks before real money.
glossary: PE / put option
A bet that Nifty will fall. Buying one pays if it falls; selling one pays you upfront and costs you if it falls.
CE / call option
A bet that Nifty will rise.
Lot
Bank Nifty options trade in lots of 30 units. ₹1 of option price = ₹30 per lot.
Put spread
Sell one put, buy a cheaper one below it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
15-min candle close
Wait for the 15-minute bar on the chart to finish before acting, so one spike doesn't fool you.
Call spread
Sell one call, buy a cheaper one above it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
